battle.name: 諸葛亮北伐
battle.brief: 建興六年（228年）春，諸葛亮率大軍出祁山，圖取關中，五年之間五次出兵，屯田渭南，直至建興十二年病歿五丈原。卡面這具羅馬投石機並未隨軍北上，但它所代表的扭力拋射技術，正是蜀漢攻城器械——車載發石車、連弩、衝車——的同源物種。

kit.name: 投石機
kit.history: 把絞盤的勢能換成一塊石頭。攻城從此有了可以計算的破壞力。

countries: 諸葛亮北伐是蜀漢與曹魏在隴右、關中一線長達六年的對峙，實際經過自建興六年（228年）春至建興十二年（234年）秋，諸葛亮先後五次出兵，最後一次病歿於五丈原。蜀漢一方以成都為都、以漢中為前進基地，丞相諸葛亮兼攬軍政，總攬北伐的戰略與器械，前線戰術多由他親自坐鎮；前方將領以關平、魏延、趙雲、馬謖、關興、張嶷、李平、王平等人為主，後方由尚書令蔣琬、侍中費禕、董允等主持政務與轉輸。蜀軍兵源主要來自益州，糧秣靠漢中沔南的屯田與成都到漢中的輸糧線接濟，最遠的一段靠木牛流馬在棧道上拖曳。蜀的目標是關中的長安與隴右三郡（南安、天水、安定），並以招撫羌氐部眾來擴大根據地。曹魏一方以洛陽為本，關中即是前線，關中大都督司馬懿與雍州方面的將領分權而制，宿將曹真、張郃、郭淮、郝昭與雍州刺史陳泰各守一線，涼州方面另有刺史與護軍經營。魏軍的長處是兵精糧足、弩甲齊備、關中屯田與洛陽轉運可以長期支撐消耗；短處是朝中曹爽與司馬懿權力分合、兵分兩處，使諸葛亮得以尋隙。兩軍的界線落在陳倉、斜谷、武功三條谷道上，這三個隘口決定了誰能把兵力與糧食送到前線。
countriesEn: The Northern Expeditions of Zhuge Liang were a six-year confrontation between Shu Han and Cao Wei along the line of Longyou and Guanzhong, running in fact from the spring of Jianxing 6 (228) to the autumn of Jianxing 12 (234), in the course of which Zhuge Liang marched out five times and was taken ill in the last campaign, dying at Wuzhangyuan. On the Shu Han side the capital was Chengdu and Hanzhong the forward base; the chancellor Zhuge Liang combined the civil and the military command, directed the strategy of the northern campaigns and their equipment personally, and sat in person over the tactical decisions in the field. The commanders in front included Guan Ping, Wei Yan, Zhao Yun, Ma Su, Guan Xing, Zhang Yi, Li Ping and Wang Ping, while at home the Minister of Works Jiang Wan, the Palace Attendant Fei Yi and Dong Yun handled administration and the flow of supplies. The troops came in the main from Yizhou, and their grain came from the farmland in southern Hanzhong and from the supply road running from Chengdu to Hanzhong, the furthest and hardest haul of all being dragged up the plank road by the wooden oxen and gliding horses. The Shu objective was the Chang'an of Guanzhong and the three commanderies of Longyou, Nan'an, Tianshui and Anding, together with the winning over of the Qiang and Di tribes to enlarge the base. On the Cao Wei side Luoyang was the centre, Guanzhong was the front line, and the commander in chief at Guanzhong, Sima Yi, shared command with the provincial commanders there: the veteran generals Cao Zhen, Zhang He, Guo Huai and Hao Zhao each held a section of the line, while Liang Province was looked after by its own inspector and Protector. Wei's strength lay in good troops and abundant grain, in its crossbows and armour, and in the fact that the farm colonies of Guanzhong and the road from Luoyang could support a long war of attrition. Its weakness was the division of authority at court between Cao Shuang and Sima Yi, and the splitting of the army between two fronts, which gave Zhuge Liang openings to exploit. The line between the two armies ran through the three passes of Chencang, Xiegu and Wugong, and it was those defiles that decided who could deliver men and grain to the front.
people: 留下姓名的核心人物當然是諸葛亮，字孔明，琅邪陽都人，早年隱居隆中，建興五年上《出師表》，劉備既死而劉禎幼弱，遂以丞相身份攬軍政，總領北伐，最終在建興十二年（234）八月病歿於五丈原軍中，時年五十四，遺命葬於褒斜谷南，軍中不設喪儀。街亭之敗的責任在馬謖：他以才器見長，亮越階拔用，命他督諸軍屯街亭，他卻舍水上山、舉措煩擾，被張郃斷其汲道而大敗，亮依軍法誅之，蔣琬以「天下未定而戮智計之士，豈不惜乎」進諫，亮答以「孫武所以能制勝於天下者，用法明也」，馬謖臨終上書自訴。魏延是先主破格提拔的西城長，北伐中的突擊主力，延曲一役以數百騎擊敗張郃部，他與長史楊儀的權力之爭是蜀中內部最深的裂痕，亮死後演成叛案。趙雲在箕谷之舉時曾被眾議疑為將反，亮力主信任，事後趙雲歎服亮的明斷。姜維是後來接棒的人：天水冀縣人，建興六年隨郤正往狄道招撫羌氐，遭魏兵包圍，他持械衝突護使者脫身，歸蜀後得亮器重，後任涼州刺史。還有李平（初名嚴平）主管漢中軍需，建興九年運糧失期被亮責貶，險些牽出蜀中兵變，楊儀在亮死後統軍退蜀。魏方留下名字的有宿將曹真（230年卒，年四十餘）、張郃（街亭破馬謖，231年追蜀軍墜澗而死，年七十餘）、關中大都督司馬懿（渭南拒亮，屢稱「亮將死矣」，其後經營關中屯田與轉運）、雍州刺史郭淮（料亮必爭芻豆，夜襲蜀營破之；後率步騎萬餘破蜀將句安於曲堤）、郝昭（以千人固守陳倉，拒蜀攻數十日）與陳泰（在雍州境內修塹設險，與郭淮共守關中）。
peopleEn: The central figure who left a name is of course Zhuge Liang, courtesy name Kongming, a native of Yangdu in Langya, who lived in seclusion at Longzhong as a young man and presented the Chu Shi Biao in the fifth year of Jianxing. After Liu Bei died and Liu Zhen was a child, Zhuge Liang took the chancellorship and the conduct of the war into his own hands, directed the northern campaigns, and in the eighth month of Jianxing 12 (234) fell ill and died in the camp at Wuzhangyuan, aged fifty-four, leaving instructions that he be buried south of Baoxie Valley and that no mourning rites be held in the army. The blame for the defeat at Jieting lay with Ma Su, who was famed for his talent, was promoted by Zhuge Liang above his rank to command the army at Jieting, and there abandoned the water and took his men up the hill in a way that threw every part of the deployment into disorder; Zhang He cut his water supply and routed him. Zhuge Liang executed him under martial law, Jiang Wan remonstrated that to slay a man of parts while the realm was still unsettled was a pity beyond measure, and Zhuge Liang answered that the reason Sun Wu was able to conquer the world was that the law was clearly applied. Ma Su wrote to him on his death bed. Wei Yan was a commoner whom the first ruler had promoted out of turn to be commandant of Xicheng, and the shock of the northern campaigns; in the fighting at Yanqu he beat Zhang He's detachment with a few hundred horsemen, and his quarrel with the chief clerk Yang Yi over command was the deepest rift inside Shu, turning after Zhuge Liang's death into a revolt. Zhao Yun was suspected by the officers at the time of the Jigu business of intending to defect, Zhuge Liang insisted on trusting him, and Zhao Yun afterwards expressed his admiration for that judgement. Jiang Wei was the man who took up the work afterwards: a native of Jixian in Tianshui, he went to Didao with Qi Zheng in the sixth year of Jianxing to win over the Qiang and Di, was surrounded by Wei troops, and broke out with his weapon in his hand to cover the escape of the envoy; joining Shu, he earned Zhuge Liang's trust and later became inspector of Liang Province. There is also Li Ping, formerly Yan Ping, who administered the military stores of Hanzhong and in the ninth year of Jianxing was censured and demoted for a late delivery of grain, a matter that came close to dragging out a mutiny in Shu, and Yang Yi, who led the army back after Zhuge Liang's death. On the Wei side the names that remain are of the veteran Cao Zhen, who died in 230 at a little over forty; Zhang He, who broke Ma Su at Jieting and in 231 was drowned in a ravine while pursuing the Shu army, aged over seventy; Sima Yi, commander in chief at Guanzhong, who faced Zhuge Liang on the Wei river and more than once reported that Liang was about to die, and who afterwards built up the farm colonies and the transport of Guanzhong; Guo Huai, inspector of Yong Province, who judged that Liang would certainly contest the fodder and grain and struck the Shu camp by night, and later led more than ten thousand foot and horse to defeat the Shu general Ju An at Qudi; Hao Zhao, who held Chencang with a thousand men and repelled Shu attacks for tens of days; and Chen Tai, who cut trenches and fortified the approaches within Yong Province and shared the defence of Guanzhong with Guo Huai.
kits: 卡面這件投石機（onager）是羅馬的老兵器，約公元前250年前後已有形制；留下最完整描述與圖樣的是維特魯威亞斯《建築十書》第十卷：木製機架以兩根夾柱夾住橫樑，橫樑上束一束扭力繩（亞麻繩浸油，或用牛筋羊腸），繩兩端拉向地面絞盤並扣住，拋臂尾端繫著皮兜，發射時解開帶扣，拋臂繞樑翻起，把石彈兜出；機身蒙皮以防火矢。石彈橫徑約四十公分、重量以數十公斤計，射程隨角度與配重而變，大致在數百步至一里之間。羅馬人自第三次布匿戰爭起以扭力砲攻城，其後隨軍遠征；埃利安《動物的特性》另記羅馬人把一具單挺投石機立在陣前，攔截敵軍衝鋒。這具兵器沒有到過中國，但拋石的技術路線在漢代中國一樣齊備：曹魏馬鈞改良發石車，傅玄《傅子》記改造之後每車所發之石可及二百步；蜀漢的車載發石車，見於裴松之注所引《襄陽記》等書記載陳式攻柳城時所用，後世稱為霹靂車。諸葛亮自己改進的連弩（一名元戎），裴注引《魏氏春秋》記「矢不及遠，非大器用，但可以神速」；木牛流馬解決的是運輸，《三國志·蜀書·諸葛亮傳》說他「性長於巧飾，損益連弩，木牛流馬，皆出其意」；裴注引《魏氏春秋》又記他集漢晉以來名刀、仿其配法造刀，五百餘柄皆有刻銘。其餘裝備以刀、劍、矛、戟、弓弩為主，護具是皮甲、札甲與木盾，攻城則靠衝車、雲梯與壕塹。
kitsEn: The piece on the card, the onager, was an old Roman weapon, a form already in existence around 250 BC; the fullest description and the only surviving drawings come from the tenth book of Vitruvius's De architectura. A wooden frame of two uprights clamps a crossbeam; a bundle of torsion ropes, hemp soaked in oil or else sinew, is fixed to that beam, its ends pulled down to windlasses at the base of the frame and held by catch releases; the throwing arm carries a sling at its tail, and when the catch is let go the arm whips over the beam and slings the stone out. The frame is covered with hides against incendiary arrows. The stones are about forty centimetres across and weigh scores of kilograms, and the range varies with the angle and the charge, roughly from several hundred paces to about a mile. The Romans used torsion artillery in sieges from the Third Punic War onward and carried it on their campaigns; Aelian, in On the Characteristics of Animals, records a single onager set up in front of a line to check a charge. This machine never came to China, but the line of technique it represents was fully present in Han China: the Cao Wei engineer Ma Jun improved the stone-throwing cart, and Fu Xuan's Fu Zi records that after his alteration the stone thrown by each cart could carry two hundred paces; the Shu Han stone-throwing vehicle, mounted on a cart, appears in the materials Pei Songzhi quotes from the Xiangyang Ji and similar books in the account of Chen Shi's attack on Liucheng, and it is what later ages call the thunder-thrower cart. The repeating crossbow that Zhuge Liang himself improved, also called the Yuanrong, is described in the Wei Shi Chunqiu quoted in Pei's commentary: it cannot shoot far, and is not a great weapon, but it can be quick. The wooden oxen and gliding horses solved transport, and the Shu Zhuan in the Zhuge Liang biography says of him that he was skilled in ingenious contrivance, that he modified the repeating crossbow and invented the wooden oxen and gliding horses, all out of his own head. The same commentary quotes a further notice that he gathered the famous blades of the Han and Jin, imitating their methods of compounding metal, and forged five hundred-odd swords, each with an inscription. The rest of the equipment consisted of sabres, swords, spears, halberds, bows and crossbows; protection was of hide armour, plated armour and wooden shields; and siege work was done with battering rams, scaling ladders and ditches.
tactics: 蜀軍的戰法是「先據險要、就糧紮營、雜以屯田、選銳突擊」四法並行。第一步是先把營壘釘在隴右的支點上：第一次出師便屯祁山堡，街亭之敗後又改從陳倉、箕谷與斜谷三個方向試探，逼魏軍分兵。第二步解決糧食：從漢中沔南屯田所得出發，用木牛流馬沿棧道北運；到了關中，就在渭南分兵耕田，實行「以資䇝糧」的長期屯墾，試圖把遠征變成駐防。第三步是分兵牽制，主力壓向祁山與武功的同時，另遣偏師（如陳式部）攻涼州柳城方向，迫魏兵不能專注一處。第四步是陣法，《三國志》說亮「推演兵法，作八陣圖」，八陣以天、地、風、雲、龍、鳥、麟、蛇為別，環環相扣，可攻可守，進退皆成陣形，行軍宿營都按陣圖布置。第五步是抓住魏軍露出的空隙反擊：延曲一役，魏延以數百騎誘敵追入谷口，回身掩殺而破張郃之眾，正是蜀軍「設伏擊敵」的典型。魏軍的應對則完全相反——不與蜀軍決戰，以守待破：郭淮判斷蜀軍必爭芻豆，便夜襲其營於上邽一帶而破之；陳泰在雍州境內修塹設險，深溝高壘以拒；郝昭以千人固守陳倉，蜀軍填壕、架雲梯、撞車攻城而終不能下。糧道是魏軍最常下手的地方，劍閣至漢中的蜀道與蜀軍前後隊之間的連絡線，都被輕騎不斷襲擾；關中一面廣設屯田積穀，一面從洛陽轉運，兵力和糧食的總量遠在蜀軍之上。
tacticsEn: The Shu method was to combine four things: seize the commanding ground first, live off the country and garrison there, till fields as well as fight, and strike with an elite picked force. The first step was to nail the camp down on a hinge of Longyou: the first expedition was based at the fortress of Qishan, and after the defeat at Jieting the army shifted to try the three approaches of Chencang, Jigu and Xiegu, forcing the Wei commanders to divide. The second step was food: starting from the farm colonies in southern Hanzhong, grain was hauled north along the plank road by wooden oxen and gliding horses; once in Guanzhong the troops were split off to till the fields along the Wei river, pursuing long-term settlement so as to turn an expedition into a garrison, and to make the army live on what the land yielded. The third step was to pin the enemy: while the main body pressed towards Qishan and Wugong, separate detachments such as Chen Shi's were sent against Liucheng in Liang Province, so that Wei troops could not concentrate. The fourth step was the array: the Shu Zhuan says that Zhuge Liang worked out the art of war and composed the Eight Formations, distinguished as Heaven, Earth, Wind, Cloud, Dragon, Bird, Qilin and Snake, linked ring to ring, able to attack and to defend, so that advance and withdrawal alike were made in formation and the marching camp itself was laid out by the plan. The fifth step was to spring on whatever the Wei army exposed: in the fighting at Yanqu, Wei Yan lured the enemy with a few hundred horsemen into the mouth of a ravine and turned to strike, breaking Zhang He's force, and that is the typical Shu ambush. The Wei response was the exact opposite, for they refused to give battle and waited to be broken: Guo Huai judged that the Shu army would certainly contest the fodder and grain, and struck its camp by night in the neighbourhood of Shangxi; Chen Tai cut trenches and set up obstacles within Yong Province, raising deep ditches and high banks against them; Hao Zhao held Chencang with a thousand men, and the Shu army filled the ditch, raised scaling ladders and brought up battering rams without ever taking the city. The supply road was where the Wei army habitually struck: the road from Jiange to Hanzhong and the line of communication between the Shu vanguard and its rear were harried continually by light horse. On the other side of the line the Wei farm colonies stored grain on a wide scale and transport came down from Luoyang, so that their total strength in men and grain stood far above that of the Shu army.
data: 可核對的數字分三類，來源可靠程度相差很大。類型一是文獻明載的：諸葛亮卒時五十四歲（《三國志·蜀書·諸葛亮傳》），曹真卒年四十餘，張郃卒年七十餘；228年街亭敗後，亮「拔西縣千餘家，遷於漢中，戮之以為警戒」，這是此役唯一精確到千位的人數記載；陳壽本傳記亮與張郃交戰時「射殺郃」，而《張郃傳》與《資治通鑑》都把張郃之死繫於231年追蜀至澗之役，兩說相牴，通行看法是亮在戰報中誇大了戰果。類型二是編年與行動的次數：第一次出師在228年春，街亭之敗在同年八月；其後228年夏再出祁山，229年屯田渭南，230年冬與曹真隔渭相持，231年春由斜谷出，234年春再出斜谷、屯武功五丈原。歷來習稱「六出祁山」，《三國志》與《資治通鑑》計數不一，實際出兵五次，其中一次是渭南的屯田對峙。類型三是推估，必須打折：每次出兵的兵數沒有可靠記載，《三國志》只作「大眾」「悉大眾」，通行估計在數萬至十餘萬之間，但其中運糧、屯田與輜重所佔比例極高，前線作戰兵力遠少於此；糧道長度方面，漢中至祁山逾千里，斜谷一線也有數百里而路途曲折，木牛的載量與行程文獻無確數，流傳說法多在每具載糧數十斛、每日行程數十里之間，可作量級參考；器械的尺度有據可查，投石機的石彈橫徑約四十公分、重量以數十公斤計，馬鈞改造後的發石車所發之石可及二百步；魏方亦有數字，《三國志·魏書·郝昭傳》記郝昭率千人固守陳倉，《郭淮傳》記其率步騎萬餘追蜀將句安於曲堤。季節與氣候同樣要計：關中雨季在七月前後，蜀軍屢選五月麥熟前後進兵，冬季棧道泥濘、糧運最難。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes of very different reliability. The first class is what the documents state outright: Zhuge Liang was fifty-four years old when he died, as the Shu Zhuan in the Zhuge Liang biography has it; Cao Zhen died at a little over forty; Zhang He died aged over seventy. After the defeat at Jieting in 228 Zhuge Liang pulled up more than a thousand households from Xixian and moved them into Hanzhong, then put them to the sword as a warning, and that is the only figure in the whole affair that is exact down to the thousand. The Zhuge Liang biography also says that in the fighting with Zhang He he shot Zhang He dead, while the Zhang He biography and the Zizhi Tongjian both place Zhang He's death in 231, in the ravine to which he pursued the Shu army; the two statements collide, and the received view is that Zhuge Liang had claimed a success in his despatch that he had not in fact won. The second class is chronology and the number of operations: the first expedition set out in the spring of 228 and Jieting fell in the eighth month of the same year; a second march out of Qishan followed in the summer of 228; the tilling of fields on the Wei river came in 229; a winter advance in 230 found the two armies facing each other across the Wei while Cao Zhen still lived; the campaign of 231 was made by way of Xiegu; and in the spring of 234 the army came out by the same road and established itself at Wuzhangyuan in Wugong. The usual phrase is that Liang marched out of Qishan six times, but the Shu Zhuan and the Tongjian do not count alike; there were in fact five expeditions, one of which was a garrison and a waiting game on the Wei river. The third class is estimate and must be discounted. No reliable figure survives for the size of any expedition: the Shu Zhuan says only that a great mass went out and that all the host went out, and the usual estimates run from tens of thousands to something over a hundred thousand, of which the proportion carried up by the transport teams, the tilling parties and the baggage was extremely high, so that the fighting strength in front was far smaller than the totals suggest. On the length of the supply line: the distance from Hanzhong to Qishan is upward of a thousand li, and the route by Xiegu runs to several hundred li and twists about; the capacity and the daily progress of the wooden oxen are not given in the documents, and the figures that circulate, of some tens of hu of grain to a machine and tens of li a day, can be used only as an order of magnitude. The dimensions of the engines are documented: the stone of an onager is about forty centimetres across and weighs scores of kilograms, and the stone thrown by Ma Jun's improved stone-throwing cart could carry two hundred paces. Wei figures survive as well: the Hao Zhao biography records that he held Chencang with a thousand men, and the Guo Huai biography that he led more than ten thousand foot and horse in pursuit of the Shu general Ju An at Qudi. Season and climate count too: the rains in Guanzhong come around the seventh month, the Shu army repeatedly chose to advance in the fifth month when the wheat ripened, and in winter the plank roads turn to mud and the grain is hardest to move.
cause: 打起來的原因有三層。最表層是蜀漢政權的生存壓力：劉備於223年去世，劉禎幼弱，諸葛亮輔政，先平南中、取得兵資，然後才圖北方；《出師表》把這層意思寫得很明白——「今天下三分，益州疲弊，此誠危急之候也」，所求者「還于舊國」，即中原。攻勢的目標是分三步：取關中長安，据隴右三郡，待關中人心震動、曹魏內部失和而圖中原。中間層是雙方的時機判斷：曹魏當時內部並不團結，曹真鎮關中、司馬懿在洛陽，兵分兩處彼此牽制，關中久經戰亂人口凋零，士氣與民政都有空隙可乘；蜀漢則有連弩、木牛流馬與漢中屯田所提供的技術條件，前進速度與後勤效率都比前人為高，所以諸葛亮判定此時可以一試。第三層是「以攻為守」的戰略哲學：蜀若一味困守益州，與關中的差距只會愈拉愈大；魏若坐擁關中，就等於掌握了統一的地理前提。蜀中對此有過正面爭論，蔣琬、費禕一派主張休養生息，諸葛亮則力主進取，兩人的分歧在北伐期間仍未調和。但所有理由都抵不過一條硬限制：蜀兵少、糧少，運糧不繼。蜀方的記錄與魏方的判斷都指向同一點——郭淮料到蜀軍必爭芻豆而夜襲其營、司馬懿屢次拒戰不決、每次北伐都以「糧盡退軍」收場，說的都是這件事。這不是可以靠將略挽回的問題，而是地理與人口決定的死結。
causeEn: There are three layers of cause. The outermost is the survival pressure on the state of Shu Han: Liu Bei died in 223, Liu Zhen was a child, and Zhuge Liang, holding the regency, first pacified the south and drew on its soldiers and stores, and only then turned towards the north. The Chu Shi Biao states that layer plainly: today the realm is divided three ways, Yizhou is worn out, and this is indeed a moment of danger; what is sought is a return to the old country, that is, to the Central Plain. The offensive was conceived in three steps: take Chang'an in Guanzhong, hold the three commanderies of Longyou, and wait for the minds of the people of Guanzhong to shake and for Cao Wei's internal discord to create the opening in which to strike the Central Plain. The middle layer is the assessment of opportunity on both sides: Cao Wei was not united within itself, Cao Zhen was stationed in Guanzhong while Sima Yi was at Luoyang, the army was split between the two and each checked the other, and Guanzhong had been so long ravaged that its population and its administration showed gaps; Shu Han meanwhile had the technical means in the repeating crossbow, the wooden oxen and gliding horses and the fields of Hanzhong, and could march and supply itself faster than those before it, so Zhuge Liang judged that the moment was worth trying. The deepest layer is the strategic philosophy of attacking in order to defend: if Shu simply sat inside Yizhou, the gap between it and Guanzhong would only widen, whereas Wei, holding Guanzhong, would hold the geographical precondition for unification. The question was argued openly in Shu: the party of Jiang Wan and Fei Yi called for resting and recuperating, Zhuge Liang insisted on the offensive, and the disagreement was still unresolved throughout the campaigns. But every argument yields to one hard limit: Shu had few men and little grain, and the grain could not be kept coming. The Shu accounts and the Wei judgements point at the same fact. Guo Huai knew that the Shu army would contest the fodder and grain and struck its camp by night; Sima Yi refused battle again and again; and every expedition ended by falling back when the grain ran out. This was not a problem that strategy could mend, but a dead knot fixed by geography and by population.
impact: 後果分幾層，最直接的一層是地理與政治格局就此固化：魏保住了關中，蜀失去關中，三國對峙的版圖從此穩定，魏得以騰手處理東吳，蜀的統一事業實際上宣告結束，而蜀漢的滅亡也由此遞進。國內層面是國力被抽乾：每次出兵都耗掉大量兵資與民夫，益州疲弊加深，後來姜維屢次出兵、諫官屢言「勞師擾民」，都源於此一開端；亮死後魏延與楊儀之爭、李平案、黃皓與姜維之隙接連爆發，北伐失敗後形成的守勢取向，把蜀推向另一種內耗。第三層是技術與思想上的遺產：連弩的「一機多矢」成為中國弩史上一條獨特的線，後來曹魏改進弩機、宋代巨石砲的拋射傳統，都能在這條線上找到源頭；木牛流馬的運輸思路，後來仍被明人徐光啟一類的農政著作引用討論；而《出師表》與「鞠躬盡瘁，死而後已」成為此後一千七百年士大夫的行為準則，《後出師表》的真偽則從明代起屢有辨偽之議。第四層是學術與考古：明、清以來對北伐成敗的論辯從未停止，王夫之、趙翼一類學者的議論至今仍被援引；陝西岐山的五丈原屯田遺址、甘肅莊浪的街亭城址與漢中劍閣一線的倉廩遺存，把這場戰爭的物質面一點點拼回來。
impactEn: The consequences work on several levels, and the most immediate is that the map was fixed: Wei kept Guanzhong, Shu lost it, the three-way division of China settled into a stable shape, Wei was freed to deal with Wu in the east, and the unification project of Shu Han was effectively over, with the fall of Shu following from it. Inside the country, the national strength was drained: each expedition consumed a great quantity of soldiers, stores and labour, the weariness of Yizhou deepened, and the later repeated campaigns of Jiang Wei, with the remonstrating officials protesting that they exhausted the people and wore out the army, all grew out of this beginning. After Zhuge Liang's death the quarrel between Wei Yan and Yang Yi, the affair of Li Ping, and the friction between Huang Hao and Jiang Wei broke out one after another, and the defensive turn that the failure of the northern campaigns produced pushed Shu into a different kind of waste. The third level is the legacy of technique and of thought. The repeating crossbow with its many bolts to a single mechanism became a distinctive strand in the history of the Chinese crossbow, from which the later improvements of Wei trigger mechanisms and the throwing tradition of the Song catapult both descend; the transport thinking of the wooden oxen and gliding horses was still quoted and discussed by agrarian writers of the Ming such as Xu Guangqi; and the Chu Shi Biao with its line about giving everything to the last of the strength became the standard of conduct for scholars and officials through seventeen hundred years, while the authenticity of the Later Chu Shi Biao has been argued over since the Ming and disputed by scholars down to the present. The fourth level is scholarly and archaeological: the debate in the Ming and the Qing over whether the northern campaigns succeeded or failed has never stopped, and the arguments of writers such as Wang Fuzhi and Zhao Yi are still cited; the Wuzhangyuan farm-colony site at Qishan in Shaanxi, the walled site of Jieting at Zhuanglang in Gansu, and the storehouses along the Jiange line in Hanzhong allow the material side of this war to be pieced back together piece by piece.
result: 五場北伐，沒有一場達到奪取關中的目標。第一場以街亭之敗收場，馬謖被斬，西縣百姓被遷走處斬，蜀軍退回漢中，此後改取陳倉、箕谷、斜谷三路試探，屢入隴右而終不能久據。第二次出師已用木牛運糧，仍因糧道不繼而退。229年屯田渭南，關中流民歸蜀，蜀軍一度逼近長安，卻在關中沒有站住腳。230年與曹真隔渭對峙，曹真同年病死，魏方前線一度鬆動，蜀軍仍未能乘隙。231年曹真反過來攻蜀，蜀軍迎戰反而在澗邊折了張郃，蜀方在關中第一次換得局部的小勝，但隨後的糧運糾紛牽出李平案，後方掣肘。234年春諸葛亮大軍出斜谷，據武功五丈原，屯田渭南，與司馬懿對峙；魏將郭淮率步騎萬餘破蜀將句安於曲堤；同年八月，亮病歿軍中，時年五十四，遺命葬於褒斜谷南，軍中不設喪儀，楊儀等整軍而還，百姓聞訊奔告，司馬懿追至其營壘，按行部伍而歎服其治軍。結果可以這樣總結：蜀軍自未攻破關中，也從未被魏軍消滅，魏的關中防線始終未破，蜀漢由攻勢轉為守勢，北伐從此成為一場在戰略上無功、在消耗上極大的持久戰；此後姜維接連北伐、耗盡國力，蜀漢的滅亡已在此時埋下伏線，而這場戰爭究竟該不該打、該不該這樣打，此後一千七百年仍是史家聚訟的題目。
resultEn: Of the five campaigns, not one achieved the object of taking Guanzhong. The first ended in the defeat at Jieting: Ma Su was executed, the people of Xixian were moved off and put to the sword, and the army fell back on Hanzhong; thereafter the three approaches of Chencang, Jigu and Xiegu were tried, and the army penetrated Longyou again and again without ever establishing itself there for long. The second expedition already used the wooden oxen for transport and still withdrew because the supply line could not keep up. In 229 the fields on the Wei river were tilled and refugees from Guanzhong came over to Shu; the army came close to Chang'an and still could not hold the ground in Guanzhong. In 230 it faced Cao Zhen across the Wei river; Cao Zhen died of illness in that year, the Wei front briefly loosened, and the Shu army still failed to exploit the gap. In 231 Cao Zhen turned and attacked Shu, the Shu army met him and lost Zhang He beside the ravine, which was the first small local gain for Shu in Guanzhong, but the quarrels over grain transport then brought the affair of Li Ping to a head and the rear began to hold the army back. In the spring of 234 Zhuge Liang led the great host out by Xiegu, established himself at Wuzhangyuan in Wugong, tilled the fields on the Wei river and faced Sima Yi; the Wei general Guo Huai led more than ten thousand foot and horse and defeated the Shu general Ju An at Qudi; and in the eighth month of that year Zhuge Liang fell ill and died in the camp, aged fifty-four, leaving instructions that he be buried south of Baoxie Valley, with no mourning rites in the army; Yang Yi and the others drew the army up and returned, word of his death spread among the people, and Sima Yi pursued to the camp and, walking through its lines, marvelled at the discipline of the host. The result can be put this way. The Shu army never broke into Guanzhong, and was never destroyed by the Wei army either; the Wei line in Guanzhong was never broken; Shu Han turned from the offensive to the defensive, and the northern campaigns became a long war that won nothing strategically and cost a great deal. Jiang Wei's repeated campaigns followed and drained what was left, and the fall of Shu Han was planted in these years; whether the war should have been fought at all, and whether it should have been fought in this way, remained a question argued by historians for the seventeen hundred years that followed.
